policy: core.review-release clauses 11, 12 and 14 (confirm_each default for commit/push, scope/risk-change invalidation of automatic authorization, PR opening/merge authorization)
scope: Approved Starter Kit roadmap only: repositories yanpenalva/starter-kit-api and yanpenalva/starter-kit-frontend. API delivery is owned in the API repository; the frontend receives the mirrored authorization when its own deliveries start. Permits reusing the validated commit/push authorization across roadmap work items and branches, and conditional execution of human-authorized merges, within these two repositories only. Early termination occurs on roadmap completion or human revocation and is recorded by a status change in this file. Any scope, branch, remote or risk change invalidates routine authorization until re-approval as core.review-release clause 12 requires.
rationale: The standing roadmap authorization recorded in .context/work/FEAT-6/approval.md (2026-10-02) grants automatic commit/push and conditional merge per delivery, while clauses 11/12/14 otherwise require separate per-item confirmations and invalidate the automatic mode on any scope change. Formalizing the deviation keeps routine roadmap delivery traceable and bounded. yanpenalva explicitly approved this exception via the question tool ('Aprovar exceção') on 2026-10-03 UTC (2026-10-02 local America/Sao_Paulo); the confirmation is recorded in the FEAT-6 approval addendum.
compensating_controls: Independent review of every delivered change before integration; an agent review is never presented as a GitHub approving review, and the author never approves their own PR with the author account.

Required checks and repository rules are verified on the exact last delivered SHA before any merge; no weakening of rules, no administrative bypass, no force push, no hard reset, no tags and no destructive Git operations.
Issue -> work item -> commit/PR traceability is required for each affected delivery, and each affected future work item MUST reference EXC-0001 in its policy_exceptions.
Per-wave gates and recorded checkpoints; the next wave starts only after the current gate passes with evidence.

Production operations, destructive commands, tags, new scope and risk changes remain excluded from routine authorization and require concrete human decisions; no forged or fake GitHub approving review is created.
Delivery and close records link this exception, and scope or risk changes invalidate routine authorization until re-approval.
